summary: Esho Yamaguchi was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University. He later held posts at Ritsumeikan University and served as a professor at Osaka University from around 1974 to 1982.
Eshun Otsuka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student (研究生) at Taisho University, where he was also attested in a research student post in 2013.

Estela Piccin works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She studied at UNICAMP, Associação Buddha-Dharma, the Methodist University of São Paulo (PhD 2022), and the Buddha-Dharma Centre of Hong Kong, holding art-related positions in Campinas and Solo Propaganda.

Ester Bianchi specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at Ca' Foscari University and EPHE under Alfredo Cadonna and Jean-Noël Robert, held posts at Venice, Florence, and Perugia, and was appointed visiting professor at UC Berkeley (2026).
Ethan Kroll is an Indology scholar who in 2012 was attested as affiliated with Baker McKenzie and serving on the editorial board of Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies.
Etienne Vermeersch (1934–2019) was a philosopher who studied at Ghent University from circa 1953 to 1965 and subsequently held an academic post there from 1967 to 1997.
Etsuaki Teraishi works in Indology and philosophy. He held posts as an associate professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and as a JSPS special researcher (attested 2001).

Eugen Ciurtin works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He has held multiple roles within the Romanian Academy, the Romanian Association for the History of Religions, and the European Association for the Study of Religions, becoming Director of the IHR in 2022.

Eugen Hultzsch was an Indologist who earned his PhD at Leipzig and studied at Bonn and under Georg Bühler. He served as Government Epigraphist in India and held academic chairs at the University of Vienna and the University of Halle.

Eugen Pander (1854–1894) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. After studying at Polytechnikum Riga and Riga Technical University, he served from 1881 to 1889 as a professor and lecturer at the Tongwen Guan.

Eugen Prym (1843–1913) specialized in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Berlin, Leipzig under Heinrich Fleischer, and Bonn under Johann Gildemeister, where he earned his PhD and became Privatdozent of Oriental Languages in 1870.

Eugen Rose (1909–2003) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who completed his education at the University of Königsberg, the University of Bonn (PhD), and the University of Marburg (dr.theol.).

Eugen Wilhelm (1842–1923) studied linguistics, Indology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies at Halle and Jena under August Schleicher. He taught at secondary schools before becoming a professor and ordinary honorary professor at the University of Jena.

Eugene N. Lane (1936–2007) was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at Princeton and Harvard before holding academic posts at the University of Virginia (circa 1962–1966) and the University of Missouri (circa 1966–2000).

Eugene Watson Burlingame (1876–1932) specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Yale, Pennsylvania, Harvard under Charles Rockwell Lanman, and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield, he served as a fellow at Pennsylvania and Johns Hopkins and lectured at Yale.

Eugene Y. Wang works in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied under Hung Wu and John M. Rosenfield, taught at the University of Chicago, and became the Abby Aldrich Rockefeller Professor of Asian Art at Harvard University.
Eugeni d'Ors (1881–1954) was a Spanish philosopher who studied at the University of Barcelona and Universidad Central, where he later held an academic post from approximately 1927 to 1953.

Eugenia Vanina is an Indologist and historian who earned her PhD from Moscow State University in 1981 and joined the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences as a researcher in 1985.

Eugenio Frola (1906–1962) was an Italian scholar active in Indology and mathematics. Educated at the Polytechnic University of Turin and University of Turin, he taught mathematics at the Polytechnic University of Turin and founded the Centro di studi metodologici di Torino.
Eugenius Marius Uhlenbeck (1913–2003) was a Dutch linguist who studied at Leiden University from circa 1932 to 1949 and served as a professor there from 1950 to 1983.
